sanskrit: yathārciṣo 'gneḥ pavanasya vegā; marīcayo 'rkasya nadīṣu cāpaḥ gacchanti cāyānti ca tanyamānās; tadvac charīrāṇi śarīriṇāṃ tu
english: As the flames of fire, the gusts of the wind, the rays of the sun, and the waters in the rivers come forth and pass away, ever streaming on, even so do the bodies of embodied beings come and go.

sanskrit: yathā ca kaś cit paraśuṃ gṛhītvā; dhūmaṃ na paśyej jvalanaṃ ca kāṣṭhe tadvac charīrodarapāṇipādaṃ; chittvā na paśyanti tato yad anyat
english: And as a man who takes up an axe sees neither smoke nor fire within the wood, so when they cleave open the body—its trunk, hands, and feet—they do not perceive that other thing which dwells within.

sanskrit: tāny eva kāṣṭhāni yathā vimathya; dhūmaṃ ca paśyej jvalanaṃ ca yogāt tadvat subuddhiḥ samam indriyatvād; budhaḥ paraṃ paśyati svaṃ svabhāvam
english: But as one who churns those very logs together would, by the proper means, see both smoke and flame, so the man of keen and disciplined intellect, gathering the senses into equipoise, perceives the Supreme, his own true nature.

sanskrit: yathātmano 'ṅgaṃ patitaṃ pṛthivyāṃ; svapnāntare paśyati cātmano 'nyat śrotrādiyuktaḥ sumanāḥ subuddhir; liṅgāt tathā gacchati liṅgam anyat
english: As in dream a man, while his own limbs lie fallen upon the earth, beholds another self of his own, so the man of clear mind and disciplined intellect, endowed with hearing and the other faculties, passes from one subtle body to another subtle body.

sanskrit: utpattivṛddhikṣayasaṃnipātair; na yujyate 'sau paramaḥ śarīrī anena liṅgena tu liṅgam anyad; gacchaty adṛṣṭaḥ pratisaṃdhiyogāt
english: That supreme embodied one is not touched by birth, growth, decay, or dissolution; yet by this subtle body, unseen, he passes to another subtle body through the working of rebirth's bond.

sanskrit: na cakṣuṣā paśyati rūpam ātmano; na cāpi saṃsparśam upaiti kiṃ cit na cāpi taiḥ sādhayate 'tha kāryaṃ; te taṃ na paśyanti sa paśyate tān
english: With the eye he does not behold the form of the Self, nor does he come into any contact with it; nor does he accomplish his ends through the senses. They do not perceive him, yet he perceives them.

sanskrit: yathā pradīpe jvalato 'nalasya; saṃtāpajaṃ rūpam upaiti kiṃ cit na cāntaraṃ rūpaguṇaṃ bibharti; tathaiva tad dṛśyate rūpam asya
english: As in a burning lamp the flame takes on some form born of its own heat, yet bears within no inner quality of visible form, even so is the form of this Self beheld.

sanskrit: yathā manuṣyaḥ parimucya kāyam; adṛśyam anyad viśate śarīram visṛjya bhūteṣu mahatsu dehaṃ; tadāśrayaṃ caiva bibharti rūpam
english: As a man, casting off his body, enters another, unseen body, so the embodied one, surrendering the body into the great elements, takes on a form that rests upon them.

sanskrit: khaṃ vāyum agniṃ salilaṃ tathorvīṃ; samantato 'bhyāviśate śarīrī nānāśrayāḥ karmasu vartamānāḥ; śrotrādayaḥ pañca guṇāñ śrayante
english: Space, wind, fire, water, and earth—the embodied one enters into them on every side; and abiding in their several seats, engaged in their works, the five faculties beginning with hearing take hold of the five sense-qualities.

sanskrit: śrotraṃ khato ghrāṇam atho pṛthivyās; tejomayaṃ rūpam atho vipākaḥ jalāśrayaḥ sveda ukto rasaś ca; vāyvātmakaḥ sparśakṛto guṇaś ca
english: Hearing arises from space, smell from earth; form is made of light, and so too is digestion; sweat and taste are declared to rest upon water; and the quality born of touch is of the nature of wind.

sanskrit: mahatsu bhūteṣu vasanti pañca; pañcendriyārthāś ca tathendriyeṣu sarvāṇi caitāni manonugāni; buddhiṃ mano 'nveti manaḥ svabhāvam
english: The five sense-objects dwell within the great elements, and the senses within those objects; all of these follow the mind, the mind follows the intellect, and the intellect follows its own essential nature.

sanskrit: śubhāśubhaṃ karma kṛtaṃ yad asya; tad eva pratyādadate svadehe mano 'nuvartanti parāvarāṇi; jalaukasaḥ srota ivānukūlam
english: Whatever deed, good or evil, has been done by him, that very deed he takes back upon himself in his own body; and high and low alike follow after the mind, as a creature of the water follows the favoring current.

sanskrit: calaṃ yathā dṛṣṭipathaṃ paraiti; sūkṣmaṃ mahad rūpam ivābhipāti svarūpam ālocayate ca rūpaṃ; paraṃ tathā buddhipathaṃ paraiti
english: As a moving thing, though minute, enters the path of sight and appears like some great form, and the eye discerns its own proper shape, so the Supreme passes into the path of the intellect.

sanskrit: manur uvāca yad indriyais tūpakṛtān purastāt; prāptān guṇān saṃsmarate cirāya teṣv indriyeṣūpahateṣu paścāt; sa buddhirūpaḥ paramaḥ svabhāvaḥ
english: Manu said: That which long remembers the sense-qualities once gathered and presented by the faculties before, even after those faculties have afterward been destroyed—that is the Supreme, whose nature is intellect.

sanskrit: yathendriyārthān yugapat samastān; nāvekṣate kṛtsnam atulyakālam yathābalaṃ saṃcarate sa vidvāṃs; tasmāt sa ekaḥ paramaḥ śarīrī
english: Since one does not apprehend all the sense-objects together at once, in their entirety and in equal time, but the knowing one moves among them according to his capacity, therefore the supreme embodied one is one alone.

sanskrit: rajas tamaḥ sattvam atho tṛtīyaṃ; gacchaty asau jñānaguṇān virūpān tathendriyāṇy āviśate śarīrī; hutāśanaṃ vāyur ivendhanastham
english: He passes through rajas, tamas, and sattva as the third—the varied qualities pertaining to knowledge; and the embodied one enters into the senses as the wind enters the fire lodged in fuel.

sanskrit: na cakṣuṣā paśyati rūpam ātmano; na paśyati sparśam indriyendriyam na śrotraliṅgaṃ śravaṇe nidarśanaṃ; tathāgataṃ paśyati tad vinaśyati
english: With the eye he does not behold the form of the Self, nor does the inner sense of the senses perceive touch, nor is the mark of hearing found within the act of hearing; whatever is so apprehended perishes.

sanskrit: śrotrādīni na paśyanti svaṃ svam ātmānam ātmanā sarvajñaḥ sarvadarśī ca kṣetrajñas tāni paśyati
english: The faculties beginning with hearing do not perceive their own selves by themselves; but the all-knowing, all-seeing Knower of the Field perceives them all.

sanskrit: yathā himavataḥ pārśvaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ candramaso yathā na dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ manujair na ca tan nāsti tāvatā
english: As the far side of the Himālaya, or the hidden face of the moon, has never been seen before by men—yet it does not therefore cease to exist—

sanskrit: tadvad bhūteṣu bhūtātmā sūkṣmo jñānātmavān asau adṛṣṭapūrvaś cakṣurbhyāṃ na cāsau nāsti tāvatā
english: so too the Self of beings, dwelling within all beings, subtle and possessed of the nature of knowledge, though never before seen by the eyes, does not therefore cease to exist.

sanskrit: paśyann api yathā lakṣma jagat some na vindati evam asti na vety etan na ca tan na parāyaṇam
english: As the world, though it sees the mark upon the moon, does not comprehend it, so the question whether this Self is or is not cannot be settled—yet it is not for that reason no refuge.

sanskrit: rūpavantam arūpatvād udayāstamaye budhāḥ dhiyā samanupaśyanti tadgatāḥ savitur gatim
english: The wise, intent upon it, though it is formless, behold with the understanding as endowed with form, at rising and at setting, the course of the sun.

sanskrit: tathā buddhipradīpena dūrasthaṃ suvipaścitaḥ pratyāsannaṃ ninīṣanti jñeyaṃ jñānābhisaṃhitam
english: Even so, by the lamp of the intellect, the truly discerning seek to bring near that which stands afar—the object of knowledge, fully gathered up within knowledge itself.

sanskrit: na hi khalv anupāyena kaś cid artho 'bhisidhyati sūtrajālair yathā matsyān badhnanti jalajīvinaḥ
english: For surely no end is attained without the proper means, as men net the fish, those creatures of the water, with snares of corded mesh.

sanskrit: mṛgair mṛgāṇāṃ grahaṇaṃ pakṣiṇāṃ pakṣibhir yathā gajānāṃ ca gajair evaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānena gṛhyate
english: As deer are caught by deer, and birds by birds, and elephants by elephants, so the object of knowledge is grasped by knowledge.

sanskrit: ahir eva hy aheḥ pādān paśyatīti nidarśanam tadvan mūrtiṣu mūrtiṣṭhaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānena paśyati
english: It is shown by the saying that only a serpent can see the feet of a serpent; even so, by knowledge one perceives the knowable that abides within embodied forms.

sanskrit: notsahante yathā vettum indriyair indriyāṇy api tathaiveha parā buddhiḥ paraṃ buddhyā na paśyati
english: As the senses cannot, even with the senses, contrive to know one another, so here the higher intellect does not behold the Supreme by intellect alone.

sanskrit: yathā candro hy amāvāsyām aliṅgatvān na dṛśyate na ca nāśo 'sya bhavati tathā viddhi śarīriṇam
english: As the moon, on the night of its dark phase, is not seen because it shows no mark, and yet suffers no destruction—so know the embodied Self to be.

sanskrit: kṣīṇakośo hy amāvāsyāṃ candramā na prakāśate tadvan mūrtiviyuktaḥ sañ śarīrī nopalabhyate
english: On the night of the dark moon, its sheath worn away, the moon does not shine forth; even so the embodied one, when parted from his bodily form, is not apprehended.

sanskrit: yathā kośāntaraṃ prāpya candramā bhrājate punaḥ tadval liṅgāntaraṃ prāpya śarīrī bhrājate punaḥ
english: As the moon, gaining a fresh sheath, shines forth once more, so the embodied one, gaining another subtle body, shines forth again.

sanskrit: janmavṛddhikṣayaś cāsya pratyakṣeṇopalabhyate sā tu candramaso vyaktir na tu tasya śarīriṇaḥ
english: Birth, waxing, and waning of it are apprehended by direct perception; but that is the manifest appearance of the moon, not of the embodied Self.

sanskrit: utpattivṛddhivyayato yathā sa iti gṛhyate candra eva tv amāvāsyāṃ tathā bhavati mūrtimān
english: As, through its arising, waxing, and waning, it is grasped as 'the moon,' so the moon, even on the dark night, remains the same possessor of form.

sanskrit: nābhisarpad vimuñcad vā śaśinaṃ dṛśyate tamaḥ visṛjaṃś copasarpaṃś ca tadvat paśya śarīriṇam
english: The darkness, whether creeping upon or releasing the moon, is not seen as it withdraws or as it approaches; behold the embodied Self in just this way.

sanskrit: yathā candrārkasaṃyuktaṃ tamas tad upalabhyate tadvac charīrasaṃyuktaḥ śarīrīty upalabhyate
english: As that darkness is apprehended when joined to moon or sun, so the Self, when joined to a body, is apprehended as 'the embodied one.'

sanskrit: yathā candrārkanirmuktaḥ sa rāhur nopalabhyate tadvac charīranirmuktaḥ śarīrī nopalabhyate
english: As Rāhu, once released from moon and sun, is no longer apprehended, so the embodied one, once freed from the body, is no longer apprehended.

sanskrit: yathā candro hy amāvāsyāṃ nakṣatrair yujyate gataḥ tadvac charīranirmuktaḥ phalair yujyati karmaṇaḥ
english: As the moon, gone into its dark phase, is still joined with the constellations, so the Self, though freed from one body, is joined with the fruits of its deeds.

sanskrit: manur uvāca yathā vyaktam idaṃ śete svapne carati cetanam jñānam indriyasaṃyuktaṃ tadvat pretya bhavābhavau
english: Manu said: As in sleep this manifest body lies still while the conscious knower roves abroad in dream, so, after death, knowledge joined with the senses passes through being and non-being.

sanskrit: yathāmbhasi prasanne tu rūpaṃ paśyati cakṣuṣā tadvat prasannendriyavāñ jñeyaṃ jñānena paśyati
english: As in clear water one beholds a reflection with the eye, so he whose senses are serene perceives the knowable through knowledge.

sanskrit: sa eva lulite tasmin yathā rūpaṃ na paśyati tathendriyākulībhāve jñeyaṃ jñāne na paśyati
english: But as that same man, when the water is troubled, does not behold the reflection, so when the senses are agitated, one does not perceive the knowable within knowledge.

sanskrit: abuddhir ajñānakṛtā abuddhyā duṣyate manaḥ duṣṭasya manasaḥ pañca saṃpraduṣyanti mānasāḥ
english: Want of understanding is wrought by ignorance; by want of understanding the mind is defiled; and when the mind is defiled, the five mental faculties are wholly corrupted.

sanskrit: ajñānatṛpto viṣayeṣv avagāḍho na dṛśyate adṛṣṭvaiva tu pūtātmā viṣayebhyo nivartate
english: He who is sated with ignorance, plunged deep in the objects of sense, does not behold the Self; but the man of purified soul turns back from those objects without having beheld it.

sanskrit: tarṣacchedo na bhavati puruṣasyeha kalmaṣāt nivartate tathā tarṣaḥ pāpam antaṃ gataṃ yathā
english: No cutting-off of thirst comes to a man here so long as his defilement remains; but when his sin has come to its end, then his thirst likewise ceases.

sanskrit: viṣayeṣu ca saṃsargāc chāśvatasya nasaṃśrayāt manasā cānyad ākāṅkṣan paraṃ na pratipadyate
english: Through clinging to the objects of sense, and through failing to take refuge in the Eternal, and through hankering with the mind after something other, a man does not attain the Supreme.

sanskrit: jñānam utpadyate puṃsāṃ kṣayāt pāpasya karmaṇaḥ athādarśatalaprakhye paśyaty ātmānam ātmani
english: Knowledge arises in men through the wearing-away of sinful deeds; and then, as in the surface of a mirror, one beholds the Self within the self.

sanskrit: prasṛtair indriyair duḥkhī tair eva niyataiḥ sukhī tasmād indriyarūpebhyo yacched ātmānam ātmanā
english: With the senses let loose a man is wretched; with those same senses restrained he is happy. Therefore let him, by the self, draw the self back from the forms presented to the senses.

sanskrit: indriyebhyo manaḥ pūrvaṃ buddhiḥ paratarā tataḥ buddheḥ parataraṃ jñānaṃ jñānāt parataraṃ param
english: Higher than the senses is the mind; higher than that is the intellect; higher than the intellect is knowledge; and higher than knowledge is the Supreme.

sanskrit: avyaktāt prasṛtaṃ jñānaṃ tato buddhis tato manaḥ manaḥ śrotrādibhir yuktaṃ śabdādīn sādhu paśyati
english: From the Unmanifest knowledge streams forth; from it the intellect, and from that the mind; and the mind, joined with hearing and the other faculties, rightly perceives sound and the rest.

sanskrit: yas tāṃs tyajati śabdādīn sarvāś ca vyaktayas tathā vimuñcaty ākṛtigrāmāṃs tān muktvāmṛtam aśnute
english: He who forsakes sound and the rest, and likewise all manifest things, and lets go the whole host of forms—he, once freed of them, partakes of the immortal.

sanskrit: udyan hi savitā yadvat sṛjate raśmimaṇḍalam sa evāstam upāgacchaṃs tad evātmani yacchati
english: As the sun, rising, sends forth its orb of rays, and that same sun, going to its setting, withdraws them back into itself,

sanskrit: antarātmā tathā deham āviśyendriyaraśmibhiḥ prāpyendriyaguṇān pañca so 'stam āvṛtya gacchati
english: so the inner Self, entering the body with the rays of the senses, and laying hold of the five sense-qualities, withdrawing them, goes to its own setting.

sanskrit: praṇītaṃ karmaṇā mārgaṃ nīyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ prāpnoty ayaṃ karmaphalaṃ pravṛddhaṃ dharmam ātmavān
english: Led again and again along the path laid out by his deeds, this self-possessed one attains the fruit of his works—dharma grown abundant.

sanskrit: viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ rasavarjaṃ raso 'py asya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate
english: For the embodied one who abstains, the objects of sense turn away, save for the relish of them; but even that relish departs once he has beheld the Supreme.

sanskrit: buddhiḥ karmaguṇair hīnā yadā manasi vartate tadā saṃpadyate brahma tatraiva pralayaṃ gatam
english: When the intellect, stripped of the qualities born of action, abides within the mind, then Brahman is attained, dissolved into that very state.

sanskrit: asparśanam aśṛṇvānam anāsvādam adarśanam aghrāṇam avitarkaṃ ca sattvaṃ praviśate param
english: Touching nothing, hearing nothing, tasting nothing, seeing nothing, smelling nothing, and without deliberation—thus the being enters the Supreme.

sanskrit: manasy ākṛtayo magnā manas tv atigataṃ matim matis tv atigatā jñānaṃ jñānaṃ tv abhigataṃ param
english: Forms are merged into the mind; the mind has passed beyond into the understanding; the understanding has passed beyond into knowledge; and knowledge has gone over into the Supreme.

sanskrit: indriyair manasaḥ siddhir na buddhiṃ budhyate manaḥ na buddhir budhyate 'vyaktaṃ sūkṣmas tv etāni paśyati
english: Through the senses the mind achieves its work, yet the mind does not know the intellect; the intellect does not know the Unmanifest; but the Subtle One perceives them all.

sanskrit: manur uvāca jñānaṃ jñeyābhinirvṛttaṃ viddhi jñānaguṇaṃ manaḥ prajñākaraṇasaṃyuktaṃ tato buddhiḥ pravartate
english: Manu said: Know that knowledge is brought to completion by the knowable; the mind has knowledge for its quality; and from the mind, joined with the instrument of wisdom, the intellect proceeds.

sanskrit: yadā karmaguṇopetā buddhir manasi vartate tadā prajñāyate brahma dhyānayogasamādhinā
english: When the intellect, endowed with the qualities of action, abides within the mind, then Brahman is discerned through the deep absorption of meditative yoga.

sanskrit: seyaṃ guṇavatī buddhir guṇeṣv evābhivartate avatārābhiniḥsrotaṃ gireḥ śṛṅgād ivodakam
english: This intellect, possessed of the qualities, moves ever among the qualities, as water streaming down in descent from a mountain peak.

sanskrit: yadā nirguṇam āpnoti dhyānaṃ manasi pūrvajam tadā prajñāyate brahma nikaṣyaṃ nikaṣe yathā
english: When the meditation that arose first within the mind attains the quality-less state, then Brahman is discerned, as gold is tested upon the touchstone.

sanskrit: manas tv apahṛtaṃ buddhim indriyārthanidarśanam na samakṣaṃ guṇāvekṣi nirguṇasya nidarśanam
english: But the mind, which has carried off the intellect and which is fixed upon the objects of sense, intent upon the qualities, cannot directly behold that which is without qualities.

sanskrit: sarvāṇy etāni saṃvārya dvārāṇi manasi sthitaḥ manasy ekāgratāṃ kṛtvā tat paraṃ pratipadyate
english: Closing fast all these gates, and standing firm within the mind, having made the mind one-pointed, one attains that Supreme.

sanskrit: yathā mahānti bhūtāni nivartante guṇakṣaye tathendriyāṇy upādāya buddhir manasi vartate
english: As the great elements turn back when their qualities are spent, so the intellect, taking up the senses, abides within the mind.

sanskrit: yadā manasi sā buddhir vartate 'ntaracāriṇī vyavasāyaguṇopetā tadā saṃpadyate manaḥ
english: When that intellect, moving within, abides in the mind, endowed with the quality of resolve, then the mind is fully formed.

sanskrit: guṇavadbhir guṇopetaṃ yadā dhyānaguṇaṃ manaḥ tadā sarvaguṇān hitvā nirguṇaṃ pratipadyate
english: When the mind, endowed with the qualities through the qualified faculties and possessing the quality of meditation, then forsakes all qualities, it attains the quality-less.

sanskrit: avyaktasyeha vijñāne nāsti tulyaṃ nidarśanam yatra nāsti padanyāsaḥ kas taṃ viṣayam āpnuyāt
english: For the discernment of the Unmanifest there is here no comparable illustration; where there is no setting down of a foot, who could reach that domain?

sanskrit: tapasā cānumānena guṇair jātyā śrutena ca ninīṣet tat paraṃ brahma viśuddhenāntarātmanā
english: By austerity and by inference, by good qualities, by birth, and by sacred learning, let a man, with wholly purified inner self, seek to draw near that supreme Brahman.

sanskrit: guṇahīno hi taṃ mārgaṃ bahiḥ samanuvartate guṇābhāvāt prakṛtyā ca nistarkyaṃ jñeyasaṃmitam
english: He who lacks the qualities follows that path only from without; for through the absence of qualities and through nature itself, the knowable is beyond reasoning, measured only against itself.

sanskrit: nairguṇyād brahma cāpnoti saguṇatvān nivartate guṇaprasāriṇī buddhir hutāśana ivendhane
english: Through quality-lessness one attains Brahman; through having qualities one is turned back; for the intellect spreads out among the qualities as fire spreads through fuel.

sanskrit: yathā pañca vimuktāni indriyāṇi svakarmabhiḥ tathā tat paramaṃ brahma vimuktaṃ prakṛteḥ param
english: As the five senses are released from their own functions, so that supreme Brahman stands released, beyond Nature.

sanskrit: evaṃ prakṛtitaḥ sarve prabhavanti śarīriṇaḥ nivartante nivṛttau ca sargaṃ naivopayānti ca
english: Thus from Nature all embodied beings arise; and when they turn back at the cessation, they no longer come into creation.

sanskrit: puruṣaḥ prakṛtir buddhir viśeṣāś cendriyāṇi ca ahaṃkāro 'bhimānaś ca saṃbhūto bhūtasaṃjñakaḥ
english: The Spirit, Nature, the intellect, the particulars and the senses, the ego-sense and self-conceit—all this, come into being, bears the name of the elemental world.

sanskrit: ekasyādyā pravṛttis tu pradhānāt saṃpravartate dvitīyā mithunavyaktim aviśeṣān niyacchati
english: The first activity of the One proceeds forth from Primal Matter; the second governs the manifestation of pairs out of the undifferentiated.

sanskrit: dharmād utkṛṣyate śreyas tathāśreyo 'py adharmataḥ rāgavān prakṛtiṃ hy eti virakto jñānavān bhavet
english: From dharma the good is drawn forth, and likewise the ill from unrighteousness; the man of passion goes back to Nature, while the dispassionate becomes possessed of knowledge.

sanskrit: manur uvāca yadā te pañcabhiḥ pañca vimuktā manasā saha atha tad drakṣyase brahma maṇau sūtram ivārpitam
english: Manu said: When your five faculties, together with the mind, are released by the five, then you shall behold that Brahman, like a thread strung through a gem.

sanskrit: tad eva ca yathā sūtraṃ suvarṇe vartate punaḥ muktāsv atha pravāleṣu mṛnmaye rājate tathā
english: And as that same thread runs again through gold, through pearls, through corals, through what is made of clay, and through what is made of silver,

sanskrit: tadvad goṣu manuṣyeṣu tadvad dhastimṛgādiṣu tadvat kīṭapataṃgeṣu prasaktātmā svakarmabhiḥ
english: so it runs through cattle and through men, through elephants, deer, and the rest, through worms and moths—the Self bound fast by its own deeds.

sanskrit: yena yena śarīreṇa yad yat karma karoty ayam tena tena śarīreṇa tat tat phalam upāśnute
english: By whatever body this one performs whatever deed, by that very body he reaps that very fruit.

sanskrit: yathā hy ekarasā bhūmir oṣadhyātmānusāriṇī tathā karmānugā buddhir antarātmānudarśinī
english: For as the earth, single in its savor, conforms itself to the nature of each plant, so the intellect follows after one's deeds, attentive to the inner Self.

sanskrit: jñānapūrvodbhavā lipsā lipsāpūrvābhisaṃdhitā abhisaṃdhipūrvakaṃ karma karmamūlaṃ tataḥ phalam
english: Desire arises preceded by knowledge; intention is preceded by desire; action is preceded by intention; and the fruit, in turn, has action for its root.
